The Case of Mr. W. Y. Char 

A MOST interesting case of the conflict of author 
ity due to the existence of consular jurisdicti 
in China was recently brought to light by the detention 
of Mr. W. Y. Char for four nights in the local police 
cell. Mr. Char was born in Honolulu and therefore 
is considered to be an American citizen. He practised} 
law in Shanghai for several years and therefore is 
supposed to know the procedures in the American court 
and the Chinese Provisional Court. Sometime ago he 
was fined $300 by the latter court on a charge of as-! 
sault. He was not satisfied and appealed the case. / 
The Court of Appeal toak the case under advisement, ; 
and because the court had refused him bail for one rea- 
son or another: he was detained in a cell in the Central! 
Police Station. Then he realised the seriousness of the! 
case, and his attorney appealed to the American Consul- 
ate for his release. On the morning when he was re-. 
leased from the cell upon the demand of the American 
Consular authorities, the Court of Appeal sat and in his 
absence sentenced him to three months’ imprisonment.' 
Though the sentence may not be enforced now that Mr. 
Char has asserted his American citizenship, he can no 
longer practice in the Provisional Court. We may have 
all the sympathy for Mr. Char as a popular member 
of the local community and as a man of high intellect 
and character but we cannot understand why he should 


| have conducted himself as a Chinese citizen under Chin- 
ese jurisdiction and then finding things not to his liking 
claimed his American citizenship. As a lawyer Mr. 
Char ought to have known exactly what his nationality 
is. If he submitted to the Provisional Court in the 
first instance without even the slightest protest, he 
should have abided by the court's judgment. Even if the : 
judgment as rendered was not just in his mind, why 
should he have appealed the case‘and having appealed why 
should he have asked for American, protection? Sup- 
posing that the Court of Appeal had dismissed the case 
in favor of Mr. Char, would he have asserted his Amer- 
ican citizenship? If the American Consular authorities 
wanted to claint Mr. Char as an American citizen, why 
did they not claim him when he appeared in the Pro- 
visional Court in the presence of an American Vice- 
Consul? When’‘a Chinese Court’s decision is favorable, 
it is upheld by the foreigner; when it is not favorable, 
then the right of extraterritoriality is asserted. This is 
but another instance of the undesirability of consular 
jurisdiction and one more reason why it should be 
abolished.

Well-yuen, known as "Nick"

visional Court.

absence. Defendant was fined
$300 in the Court of First In-
stance, but this was changed
to three months' imprisonment
yesterday.
In connection with this case,
it is understood that Messrs.
H. E. Stevens and C. D.
Meinhardt, American Vice-
Consuls and the Senior Con-
sul's Deputy, endeavoured to
see Mr. Wunat King, Com-
missioner of Foreign Affairs,
on appointment, but upon ar-
rival at the bureau were in-
formed that the Commissioner
was not in.

《上海泰晤士报》，1929年2月9日，星期六。

对“尼克”·查的判决

上诉法院无视被告的公民身份。

查威元（Char Well-yuen）先生，人称“尼克”·查（"Nick" Char），因在先施公司游乐场（Pioneer Field）协助一起严重斗殴事件并袭击一名华人，被临时法院判处刑罚。鉴于上诉法院无视查先生作为美国公民的身份，此案引起了广泛关注。经总领事 R. S. Cunningham 先生干预，查先生得以从警方羁押中获释。查先生出生于檀香山，系华人，是美国律师协会成员。因此，他不受临时法院的管辖。

尽管事实如此，由钟法官主持的临时上诉法院昨日仍在查先生缺席的情况下审理了此案。被告在初审法院被罚款300美元，但昨日该判决被改为三个月监禁。

据悉，与此案有关的是，美国副领事 H. E. Stevens 和 C. D. Meinhardt 先生以及高级领事代理曾试图按预约会见外交事务局局长 Wunat King 先生，但到达该局时被告知局长不在。

（批：IV B. I. D. Reg. 请归档，并在“88/立法”项下交叉归档。1929年2月25日。）

THE CHINA CRITIC February 21, 1929

The Case of Mr. W. Y. Char
A MOST interesting case of the conflict of authority due to the existence of consular jurisdiction in China was recently brought to light by the detention of Mr. W. Y. Char for four nights in the local police cell. Mr. Char was born in Honolulu and therefore is considered to be an American citizen. He practised law in Shanghai for several years and therefore is supposed to know the procedures in the American court and the Chinese Provisional Court. Sometime ago he was fined $300 by the latter court on a charge of assault. He was not satisfied and appealed the case. The Court of Appeal took the case under advisement, and because the court had refused him bail for one reason or another he was detained in a cell in the Central Police Station. Then he realised the seriousness of the case, and his attorney appealed to the American Consulate for his release. On the morning when he was released from the cell upon the demand of the American Consular authorities, the Court of Appeal sat and in his absence sentenced him to three months' imprisonment. Though the sentence may not be enforced now that Mr. Char has asserted his American citizenship, he can no longer practice in the Provisional Court. We may have all the sympathy for Mr. Char as a popular member of the local community and as a man of high intellect and character but we cannot understand why he should
have conducted himself as a Chinese citizen under Chinese jurisdiction and then finding things not to his liking claimed his American citizenship. As a lawyer Mr. Char ought to have known exactly what his nationality is. If he submitted to the Provisional Court in the first instance without even the slightest protest, he should have abided by the court's judgment. Even if the judgment as rendered was not just in his mind, why should he have appealed the case and having appealed why should he have asked for American protection? Supposing that the Court of Appeal had dismissed the case in favor of Mr. Char, would he have asserted his American citizenship? If the American Consular authorities wanted to claim Mr. Char as an American citizen, why did they not claim him when he appeared in the Provisional Court in the presence of an American Vice-Consul? When a Chinese Court's decision is favorable, it is upheld by the foreigner; when it is not favorable, then the right of extraterritoriality is asserted. This is but another instance of the undesirability of consular jurisdiction and one more reason why it should be abolished.

查威元先生案

由于在中国存在领事裁判权而导致的管辖权冲突，最近通过查威元（W. Y. Char）先生在当地警察拘留所被关押四晚一事显露出来，这是一个非常有趣的案例。查先生出生于檀香山，因此被视为美国公民。他在上海执业律师多年，因此理应熟悉美国法院和中国临时法院的程序。不久前，他因袭击指控被后者法院罚款300美元。他对此不满并提起上诉。上诉法院受理了此案，但由于法院以某种理由拒绝了他的保释申请，他被关押在中央巡捕房的牢房中。随后他意识到了案件的严重性，其律师向美国领事馆求助要求释放他。在美国领事当局要求下，他于早晨从牢房获释，当天上午上诉法院开庭，并在他缺席的情况下判处他三个月监禁。虽然既然查先生已主张其美国公民身份，该判决目前可能无法执行，但他再也无法在临时法院执业。我们对查先生作为当地社区中受欢迎的一员，以及作为一名具有高智商和高尚品格的人，表示同情，但我们无法理解他为何在以中国公民身份接受中国司法管辖行事，并在发现结果不合心意时又声称其美国公民身份。作为一名律师，查先生应该确切知道他的国籍是什么。如果他在初审时毫无异议地服从临时法院的管辖，他就应该遵守法院的判决。即使他认为判决不公，为何又要上诉？既已上诉，为何又寻求美国保护？假如上诉法院驳回了针对查先生的案件，他还会主张其美国公民身份吗？如果美国领事当局想要主张查先生是美国公民，为何不在他出现在有美国副领事在场的临时法院时提出这一主张？当中国法院的判决有利时，外国人予以支持；当判决不利时，则主张治外法权权利。这不过是领事裁判权令人不悦的又一个例证，也是应当废除它的又一个理由。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 9, 1929

THE CASE OF "NICK" CHAR
Fine of $300 Changed to Three Months Imprisonment by Court of Appeal Despite Mr. Char's Citizenship

LAWYER REMOVED FROM POLICE CUSTODY

Considerable interest is now being centred on the case of Char Wai-yuen ("Nick" Char), a Chinese who was born in Honolulu and who is a member of the American Bar, which has brought about international complications.

The detention of Mr. Char was the subject of a very strong statement in Court on Thursday by Mr. H. E. Stevens, the U. S. Vice-Consul and Senior Consul's Deputy, but, in spite of this, Mr. Char was yesterday afternoon sentenced to three months' imprisonment by the Provisional Court of Appeals. However, he was removed from the custody of the Municipal Police by the United States Consular authorities under instructions from Mr. E. S. Cunningham, the American Consul-General, who held that Mr. Char, being an American citizen, was not subject to the Provisional Court or any court other than the United States Court for China.

After Mr. Char had been removed from Central Police Station, Mr. Cunningham was questioned by a representative of this paper and he stated that the news was quite correct. Mr. Char, he said, was an American citizen and he would be protected by the American laws.

U. S. Consul-General's Attitude

Asked whether he would agree to allow Mr. Char to submit to the jurisdiction of the Provisional Court, Mr. Cunningham said, "Decidedly no." Mr. Char, he reiterated, could be sued in the U. S. Court for China if the Chinese complainant so wished.

The Chinese judges of the Provisional Court differ in opinion from Mr. Cunningham for they informed the "North-China Daily News" representative that, according to Chinese law, Mr. Char is a Chinese citizen. The fact that he was born in a foreign country did not affect his Chinese status and the judgment of the Court would have to be enforced. It was an unfortunate matter, but the law had to take its course.

Mr. Char was to have appeared before Judges Chung (presiding) Tsing and Chiu in the Provisional Court of Appeals yesterday afternoon but, owing to the fact that he had been removed from the custody of the police by the American Consular officials, he failed to put in an appearance, so the case was proceeded with in his absence, Judge Chung saying:—

This case was set for 2 p.m. and it is now 3 p.m. and accused is not here. According to article 325 of the code, judgment can be given in the absence of accused and the police can inform accused of the Court's judgment.

According to the facts of the case, the complainant has been seriously injured but, according to the law, he was not and consequently accused is sentenced for causing slight injury.

In the Court of First Instance, accused was fined $300. To a poor man this would be heavy punishment but, as accused is a rich man, this fine is no punishment so he is sentenced to imprisonment.

Complainant's friend said that complainant's injury may get worse later on, but Judge Chung said that the Court could not wait for that to happen.

The Court then rendered judg
(Continued on Page 18)

THE CASE OF "NICK" CHAR
(Continued from Page 11)

ment as follows:—The original judgment is set aside. Accused is sentenced to three months' imprisonment for assault on complainant. Accused's appeal is dismissed. Each two days of his detention shall count as one in prison.

It appears, in connection with Mr. Char's release by the American authorities, that Mr. Cunningham wrote letters to the Commissioner of Foreign Affairs and to the President of the Provisional Court demanding Mr. Char's release. Mr. Cunningham, we understand, drew attention to article 11 of the treaty of 1858 between China and the United States which provided that American citizens charged with offences could only be brought before the American authorities and charged according to the laws of the United States.

Mr. Char Released

Failing to receive a satisfactory response and as Mr. Char was not released, Mr. Cunningham addressed a letter to Mr. S Fessenden, chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, which resulted in Mr. Char's release.

Prior to his release, however, Messrs. H. E. Stevens and C. D. Meinhardt, American Vice-Consuls and Senior Consul's Deputies, went to the Bureau of Foreign Affairs, on appointment, to see Mr. Wunsz King, the Commissioner. They were informed, however, that he was not in and, therefore, they did not see him.

《字林西报》，1929年2月9日，星期六

“尼克”·查案

尽管查先生拥有公民身份，上诉法院仍将300美元罚款改为三个月监禁

律师被移出警方羁押

目前，人们的兴趣集中在查威元（“尼克”·查）一案上，此人是出生于檀香山的华人，也是美国律师协会成员，该案已引发国际纠纷。

周四，美国副领事兼高级领事代理 H. E. Stevens 先生在法庭上发表了一份非常强烈的声明，谈及查先生的拘留问题，但尽管如此，查先生仍于昨日下午被临时上诉法院判处三个月监禁。然而，根据美国总领事 E. S. Cunningham 先生的指示，美国领事当局将查先生从工部局警务处的羁押中移出，Cunningham 先生认为，查先生作为美国公民，不受临时法院或除美国在华法院以外的任何法院的管辖。

查先生被从中央巡捕房移走后，本报代表询问了 Cunningham 先生，他表示消息完全属实。他说，查先生是美国公民，将受到美国法律的保护。

美国总领事的立场

当被问及是否同意让查先生接受临时法院的管辖时，Cunningham 先生说：“坚决不同意。”他重申，如果中国原告愿意，可以在美国在华法院起诉查先生。

临时法院的中国法官与 Cunningham 先生意见相左，他们告诉《字林西报》代表，根据中国法律，查先生是中国公民。他出生在外国这一事实并不影响他的中国身份，法院的判决必须执行。这是一件不幸的事，但法律必须按其程序进行。

查先生原定于昨日下午在临时上诉法院出庭，由钟法官（主持）、青法官和邱法官审理，但由于他已被美国领事官员从警方羁押中移出，未能出庭，因此案件在他缺席的情况下进行审理，钟法官说：—

本案定于下午2点开庭，现在已是下午3点，被告不在场。根据法典第325条，可以在被告缺席的情况下作出判决，警方可以将法院的判决通知被告。

根据案情，原告受了重伤，但根据法律，并非如此，因此被告因造成轻伤被判刑。

在初审法院，被告被罚款300美元。这对穷人来说是沉重的惩罚，但由于被告是富人，这笔罚款不算惩罚，所以他被判处监禁。

原告的朋友说，原告的伤势日后可能会恶化，但钟法官说，法院不能等待这种情况发生。

法院随后作出判
（续至第18页）

“尼克”·查案
（续自第11页）

决如下：—原判撤销。被告因袭击原告被判处三个月监禁。驳回被告上诉。其被拘留每两天折抵一天刑期。

据悉，关于美国当局释放查先生一事，Cunningham 先生曾致函外交事务局局长和临时法院院长，要求释放查先生。据了解，Cunningham 先生提请注意1858年中美条约第11条，该条规定，被指控犯罪的美国公民只能由美国当局审讯，并根据美国法律提出指控。

查先生获释

由于未得到满意答复且查先生未被释放，Cunningham 先生致函上海工部局董事会主席 S. Fessenden 先生，此举导致查先生获释。

然而，在获释之前，美国副领事兼高级领事代理 H. E. Stevens 和 C. D. Meinhardt 先生曾按预约前往外交事务局会见局长 Wunsz King 先生。但他们被告知局长不在，因此未能见到他。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 8, 1929

AMERICAN CITIZEN'S
STATUS

Defined by Deputy When Hawaii-
ian Born Lawyer Appears
Before Judge

A comprehensive statement was
made by Mr. H. E. Stevens, U. S.
Vice-Consul and Senior Consul's
Deputy, in the Shanghai Provisional
Court yesterday with reference to
the status of Char Wai-yuen ("Nick
Char"), a lawyer, who is associated
with Mr. H. D. Rodger.

Mr. Char was charged with
assaulting a Chinese on the Pioneer
Field.

In Court yesterday, Mr. Rodger
drew the attention of the Court
(Judge Shen and Mr. Stevens) to
the fact that Mr. Char was an
American citizen, born in Honolulu,
Territory of Hawaii, and therefore
he was not subject to the jurisdiction
of the Provisional Court or other
Chinese court. Mr. Char, continued
counsel, had been a member of the
American Bar for the past six
years, and Mr. Rodger had proof
showing that he was born in Hawaii.
This was shown on his Army dis-
charge certificate, Mr. Char having
served with the American Forces
in France during the Great War.
"Why he has surrendered himself to
this Court does not matter," Mr.
Rodger said, "He cannot be made
to appear before this Court unless
he has expatriated himself."

Not a Chinese Lawyer

Judge Shen—This case is pending
in the Court of Appeals, so we
cannot deal with it.

Mr. Rodger—That makes no
difference. Mr. Char is not required
to appear before this Court, nor
should he have appeared before the
Appeal Court. He is not a Chinese
lawyer. He is an American lawyer.
He has done nothing to make him
lose his American citizenship, there-
fore the question of his citizenship
can be raised in this Court at any
time, no matter if the case is pend-
ing in the Court of Appeals or not.

Mr. R. T. Bryan (Prosecuting
Solicitor who appeared for the
Police) said that he would like the
Court to note that, if the Municipal
Council received a letter from the
American Consul-General saying
that Mr. Char was an American
citizen, the Police would have no
other alternative but to hand him
over to the American Court but up
to the present no such notification
had been received.

Mr. Stevens—If Mr. W. Y. Char
was born in the United States, and
was subject to the jurisdiction
thereof, he is a citizen of the United
States, provided, he has not ex-
patriated himself by becoming
naturalized in any foreign state in
conformity with the law of that
state or by taking an oath of
allegiance to any foreign state.

A Citizen's Rights and Privileges

The rights and privileges of a
citizen of the United States, Mr.
Stevens continued, cannot be denied
or abridged on account of race or
colour.

Under the treaties, citizens of the
United States in China (the state-
ment continued), who wound the
persons of Chinese, shall be punished
only by the Consul or other public
functionary thereto authorized,
according to the laws of the United
States. But arrests in order to
trial may be made by the Chinese.

If Mr. Char is an American
citizen, Mr. Stevens continued, he
may be detained in Chinese custody
pending a requisition from the
American Consul to have him hand-
ed over to the jurisdiction of the
United States Court for China.

Mr. Rodger asked that the
Deputy's statement be endorsed on
the charge sheet (which was done),
so that no other action could be
taken against Mr. Char in the Pro-
visional Court.

Judge Shen said that he agreed
with what Mr. Stevens had said,
but he failed to mark the Chinese
charge sheet.

Mr. Bryan—I understand that
the Police must hold Mr. Char until
they receive information from the
United States Consul-General say-
ing that Mr. Char is an American
citizen.

Judge Shen—That is so, Mr.
Bryan.

This concluded the hearing.

Mr. Char, as he Anglicized his
name, was born in Honolulu in 1898
of unnaturalized Chinese parents,
attended university in that city,
and was among the first to volunteer
for service in France in 1917. At
that time he was a freshman. Over-
seas he was engaged in three major
conflicts, and after the Armistice,
attended a university for one year.
Upon returning to America he com-
pleted his law course in Creighton
University, Omaha, Nebraska,
received his bachelor-of-law degree,
and was admitted to the Nebraska
Bar. It is understood that Mr.
Char has registered at the Ameri-
can Consulate yearly for the past
six years.

《字林西报》，1929年2月8日，星期五

美国公民身份

夏威夷出生律师出庭受审时由副领事界定身份

昨日，美国驻上海副领事兼高级领事代理人 H. E. Stevens 先生在上海临时法院就律师 Char Wai-yuen（“Nick Char”，与 H. D. Rodger 先生有合作关系）的身份问题发表了全面声明。

Char 先生被控在先锋球场（Pioneer Field）袭击一名华人。

在昨日的庭审中，Rodger 先生提请法庭（沈法官和 Stevens 先生）注意，Char 先生是美国公民，出生于夏威夷领地檀香山，因此不受临时法院或其他中国法院的管辖。辩护律师继续指出，Char 先生在过去六年中一直是美国律师协会的成员，且 Rodger 先生持有证明其出生于夏威夷的证据。这一事实显示在其军队退伍证书上，Char 先生曾在大战期间随美军在法国服役。“他为何自愿向本庭投案并不重要，”Rodger 先生说，“除非他已放弃国籍，否则不能强迫他出现在本庭面前。”

并非中国律师

沈法官：此案正在上诉法院审理中，故我们无法处理。

Rodger 先生：这没有区别。Char 先生无需出现在本庭面前，他也不应出现在上诉法院面前。他不是中国律师。他是美国律师。他没有任何行为导致其丧失美国公民身份，因此无论案件是否正在上诉法院审理，均可在本庭提出其公民身份问题。

R. T. Bryan 先生（代表警方出庭的公诉律师）表示，他希望法庭注意到，如果工部局收到美国总领事来函称 Char 先生为美国公民，警方将别无选择，只能将其移交给美国法院，但截至目前尚未收到此类通知。

Stevens 先生：如果 W. Y. Char 先生出生于美国并受其管辖，那么他就是美国公民，前提是他未通过依照该国法律归化入籍任何外国或向任何外国宣誓效忠而放弃国籍。

公民的权利与特权

Stevens 先生继续说道，美国公民的权利和特权不得因种族或肤色而被剥夺或限制。

根据条约，在华美国公民（声明继续指出）若致伤华人，仅能由领事或经授权的其他公职人员依据美国法律予以惩处。但中方可以进行逮捕以便审判。

Stevens 先生继续说，如果 Char 先生是美国公民，他可以由中国方面拘留，等待美国领事提出要求，将其移交给美国驻华法院管辖。

Rodger 先生请求将副领事的声明背书于起诉书上（已照办），以便临时法院不再对 Char 先生采取其他行动。

沈法官表示同意 Stevens 先生的说法，但他未在中文起诉书上进行标注。

Bryan 先生：我理解警方必须扣留 Char 先生，直到收到美国总领事关于 Char 先生是美国公民的通知为止。

沈法官：是这样，Bryan 先生。

听证至此结束。

Char 先生（这是他的英文化名）于1898年出生于檀香山，父母为未入籍的华人，他在该市就读大学，并于1917年成为最早志愿赴法服役的人员之一。当时他还是一名大一新生。在海外期间，他参加了三次重大战役，停战后又在大学就读一年。回到美国后，他在内布拉斯加州奥马哈的克雷顿大学（Creighton University）完成了法律课程，获得法学学士学位，并取得内布拉斯加州律师资格。据悉，Char 先生在过去六年中每年都在美国领事馆登记。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 7, 1929.

W. Y. Char To Appear Before
Provisional Court To-day

An appeal to the American Con-
sular authorities in the case of Mr.
W. Y. Char, local Chinese-Ameri-
can attorney, has been made by
Mr. H. D. Rodger, who is repre-
senting Mr. Char. The latter spent
his third consecutive night in a
cell at the Central Police Station
last night and this morning is to
appear in the Provisional Court
where the matter of his nation-
ality will be brought up and
efforts made by his legal repre-
sentative to have him turned over
to the American authorities.

Mr. Char, as was reported yes-
terday in this newspaper, was
found guilty in the Provisional
Court on a charge of assaulting a
Chinese youth. He was fined $300
and appealed the case. The Court
of Appeals has the case under ad-
visement.

The attorney, it was learned
yesterday, is a bona fide American
citizen, although he is a Chinese.
He was born in Honolulu. Under
the laws of China, it was stated
yesterday, he has a dual nation-
ality and is both an American and
a Chinese citizen. Just whether
he is subject to the laws of both

nations is problematical.
In submitting himself for trial
in the Provisional Court Mr. Char
is understood to have acted con-
trary to the warning of Mr. C. D.
Meinhardt, American Vice-Consul
and Senior Consul's Deputy at the
Provisional Court. Because of his
American citizenship the attorney
is stated to have been advised to
submit only to the jurisdiction of
the American Court for China.

Mr. Meinhardt and Mr. Rodger
yesterday visited the prisoner in
his cell at the Central Station. Fol-
lowing their conference Mr. Mein-
hardt declined to discuss the case
stating that no decision has been
reached in the matter and that the
case is being considered by the
proper authorities.

《上海泰晤士报》，1929年2月7日，星期四

W. Y. Char 今日将出庭临时法院

H. D. Rodger 先生代表当地华裔美籍律师 W. Y. Char 先生，已向美国领事当局提出上诉。后者昨晚在中央巡捕房牢房中度过了连续第三个夜晚，今晨将在临时法院出庭，届时将提出其国籍问题，其法律代表将努力将其移交给美国当局。

正如本报昨日报道，Char 先生在临时法院被裁定犯有袭击一名中国青年罪。他被罚款300元并提起上诉。上诉法院正在审议此案。

据悉，该律师虽为华人，但是货真价实的美国公民。他出生于檀香山。昨日有人指出，根据中国法律，他拥有双重国籍，既是美国公民也是中国公民。他是否同时受两国法律管辖，尚存疑问。

据悉，Char 先生自愿接受临时法院审判的行为，违背了美国驻临时法院副领事兼高级领事代理人 C. D. Meinhardt 先生的警告。鉴于其美国公民身份，据称已建议该律师仅接受美国驻华法院的管辖。

Meinhardt 先生和 Rodger 先生昨日前往中央巡捕房牢房探视了这名囚犯。会谈后，Meinhardt 先生拒绝讨论此案，称此事尚未作出决定，有关当局正在审议中。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 1929.

SHANGHAI ATTORNEY
IS GAOLED

Judge Refuses To Allow
Cash Bail For Mr.
W. Y. Char

Owing to the refusal of a
Chinese Judge of the Shangha:
Court of Appeals to allow cash or
shop bail, Mr. W. Y. Char, local
attorney, spent last night in a cell
at the Central Police Station. Mr.
Char, who is familiarly known as
"Nick" to his fellow lawyers,
also spent Monday night in the
same call.
Mr. Char, who is stated to be
an American-born Chinese and an
American citizen, has many times
appeared as a lawyer in the court
of the very Judge who refused
him liberty on bail. Mr. Char has
also appeared innumerable times
as an attorney in cases in the
American Court for China, and in
the Provisional Court. It was in
the latter court that he was con-
victed sometime ago on a charge
of assault. In his legal profession
he is associated with Mr. H. D.
Rodger, one of the leading mem-
bers of the local American Bar.
The history of Mr. Char's case
and subsequent imprisonment dates
back to an afternoon of June 4,
1927. The attorney, who is known
for his athletic prowess, repaired
to Pioneer Field on that after-
noon to engage in baseball prac-
tice. He was joined by three
other men, all foreign-born
Chinese.

Lost Baseball
At the same time about 15
young Chinese were playing foot-
ball on the field. After practic-
ing an hour or two Mr. Char and
his companions elected to go to
the dressing room, leaving one of
the quartette on the field to
search for a lost baseball.
According to the evidence pro-
duced in the Provisional Court at
the time of the trial, the fourth
member of the party found that
a Chinese youth had stolen the
baseball, secreting it in a base-
ball glove. The youth is stated
to have refused to surrender the
ball, resulting in it being forcibly
taken from him by Mr. Char's
friend.
The youth is asserted to have
been slapped by the elder man,
following which the football
players took a hand and are
stated to have driven the base-
ball player from the field, using
stones and fists in the process.

Fled From Field
The latter is reported to have
fled to the dressing room of the
field and reported the matter to
Mr. Char and the others. Joined
by Mr. Paul Kong, the five are
reported to have returned to the
field to demand an explanation
from the football players.
The football players, it is
claimed, addressed the five in

Chinese, which was not understood,
the five baseball players replying
in English, stated not to have
been understood by the football
players.
An argument followed and re-
sulted in a free-for-all fight.
In court Mr. Char testified that
the football players were armed
with at least two bamboo poles,
and that during the struggle one
of the pole-bearers swung at one
of the baseball players, missed
him and instead struck a young
Chinese allied with the football
players.

Sustained Severe Injuries
The Chinese youth sustained a
fractured jaw and other injuries,
necessitating immediate medical
attention. The fight ended and
the injured youth was hurried to
the St. Maria Hospital by Mr.
Char and Mr. Kong.
Two weeks later Mr. Char re-
ceived a summons from the Pro-
visional Court, ordering him to
appear and answer to a charge of
assault. The case was remanded
from time to time and finally came
to trial about three months ago,
at which time Mr. Char was found
guilty and fined $300.
He appealed the case through
his attorneys, Messrs. D. S. Chen
and S. C. Yang. The case came
before the Court of Appeals on
Monday, Judge Chung ordering
that Mr. Char be remanded in
custody and denying cash or shop
bail.

Cash Bail Offered
Friends of the attorney offered
to put up a cash bail of $10,000
but this is stated to have been
refused by Judge Chung, who
ordered that the convicted man
be lodged in gaol. Mr. Char was
taken to Central Police Station.
Last night and on Monday night
he slept in a cell housing a number
of armed robbers and other
criminals.
After receiving the court sum-
mons and prior to the time he was
brought before the Court of Ap-
peals, Mr. Char was at liberty on
his own recognizance. He was
convicted and fined in the Pro-
visional Court by Judge Chau.
Judgment in the case has not been
handed down by the Court of
Appeals.

Born In Honolulu
Mr. Char was born in Honolulu,
where he practiced law before
coming to this city, and is stated
to be an American citizen. It
was learned yesterday that the
case has been called to the atten-
tion of the American authorities.
It is understood that the injured
Chinese has not yet fully recover-
ed. In court, it was testified by
a foreign doctor that the injured
man left the hospital before he
should have done so and that had
he remained two months he would
have fully recovered from his
injuries.
The contention of the complain-
ant is that he was attacked and
brutally beaten.

《上海泰晤士报》，1929年2月6日，星期三

上海律师入狱

法官拒绝允许 W. Y. Char 先生缴纳现金保释

由于上海上诉法院的一名中国法官拒绝允许缴纳现金或铺保，当地律师 W. Y. Char 先生昨晚在中央巡捕房的牢房中度过。Char 先生在同行律师中熟称为“Nick”，周一晚上他也睡在同一间牢房里。

据称 Char 先生是生于美国的华人及美国公民，他曾多次在那位拒绝其保释自由的法官所在的法庭上以律师身份出庭。Char 先生也曾无数次在美国驻华法院和临时法院的案件中以律师身份出庭。正是在后一法院，他不久前因袭击罪被定罪。在法律职业上，他与当地美国律师界的杰出成员之一 H. D. Rodger 先生合作。

Char 先生案件及其随后被监禁的历史可追溯至1927年6月4日下午。这位以运动才能著称的律师当天下午前往先锋球场进行棒球练习。另有三名男子加入了他，他们均为外籍出生的华人。

丢失棒球

与此同时，约有15名中国青年正在场上踢足球。练习了一两个小时后，Char 先生及其同伴决定去更衣室，留下四人中的一人在场上寻找丢失的棒球。

根据审判时在临时法院提出的证据，该团体的第四名成员发现一名中国青年偷走了棒球，并将其藏在棒球手套里。据称该青年拒绝交出球，结果被 Char 先生的朋友强行夺回。

据称，这名青年被那位年长者扇了耳光，随后足球运动员介入，据称他们用石头和拳头将棒球运动员赶出了球场。

逃离球场

据报道，后者逃至球场更衣室，并将此事报告给 Char 先生和其他人。据报道，Paul Kong 先生加入后，五人返回球场，要求足球运动员给出解释。

据称，足球运动员用中文与五人交谈，但五人听不懂；五名棒球运动员用英语回答，据称足球运动员也听不懂。

随后发生争吵，并演变成一场混战。

在法庭上，Char 先生作证说，足球运动员至少持有两根竹竿，在争斗过程中，其中一名持竿者挥向一名棒球运动员但未击中，反而击中了一名与足球运动员一方有关的年轻华人。

遭受重伤

这名中国青年下颌骨折并受其他伤，需要立即就医。打斗结束，受伤青年由 Char 先生和 Kong 先生急忙送往圣玛利亚医院（St. Maria Hospital）。

两周后，Char 先生收到临时法院的传票，命令其出庭应诉袭击指控。该案多次延期，最终在大约三个月前开庭审理，当时 Char 先生被裁定有罪并罚款300元。

他通过其律师 D. S. Chen 和 S. C. Yang 先生提起上诉。该案于周一提交上诉法院，钟法官命令将 Char 先生还押候审，并拒绝现金或铺保。

提供现金保释

该律师的朋友愿意提供10,000元现金保释，但据称被钟法官拒绝，法官命令将这名被判刑者收监。Char 先生被带往中央巡捕房。昨晚和周一晚上，他睡在一间关押着多名武装抢劫犯和其他罪犯的牢房里。

在收到法院传票后至被带上上诉法院之前，Char 先生具结释放。他由周法官在临时法院定罪并罚款。上诉法院尚未对该案作出判决。

出生于檀香山

Char 先生出生于檀香山，在来到本市之前曾在那里执业律师，据称是美国公民。昨日获悉，此案已提请美国当局注意。

据悉，受伤的华人尚未完全康复。在法庭上，一名外籍医生作证说，伤者过早离开了医院，如果他多住两个月，伤势本可完全痊愈。

原告的主张是，他遭到袭击并被残忍殴打。
